newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Jail terms sought for S.Korean student protesters.
newsitem.headline: Jail terms sought for S.Korean student protesters.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors sought prison terms for 17 of 241 students who went on trial on Tuesday in connection with violent campus demonstrations in August, the domestic Yonhap news agency reported.
State prosecutors in Seoul District Court said the 17 should spend 2-1/2 to three years in jail for their role in the protests at Seoul's Yonsei University, Yonhap said.
Court officials were unavailable for comment on the report.

About 3,225 students were arrested after riot police stormed the campus in August to end seven days of occupation by the students who were demanding reunification with North Korea and the withdrawal of U.S. troops stationed in South Korea.

A total of 444 students have been charged in connection with the demonstrations -- the worst since President Kim Young-sam took power in February 1993. Yonhap said 241 of those students went on trial on Tuesday and the remainder go on trial on Thursday.

Thirty-eight students face charges under the National Security law which bars all unapproved contacts with North Korea, while 10 have been charged in connection with the murder of a policeman who died of head wounds during the protests.
The remaining students face charges over their involvement in the demonstrations.
Yonhap said sentencing was likely on October 29.
